content.text:
All three sub-agents are back, and I caught and corrected one of my own mistakes before writing this up (see the `crossSiteUrl.ts` block). Full reconciliation below.

## Scale line

Plan (`~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-831/plan.md` §Step C1) calls this step **Heavy**: run all six predicate branches explicitly, exercise both Safari-private-mode throw paths, capture fail-on-purpose reds for all three new test files. I ran 4 angles (gates-from-scratch, and one deep-dive per source file) via 3 dispatched sub-agents plus my own direct work, matching that weight. From the standard 10-angle framework I dropped six as vacuous for this step and say so: **Tokens** (zero `var(--zimm-*)` usage anywhere in these files), **Styling conformance** (no CSS/recipe files), **Accessibility** (no JSX/DOM output), **Story interactivity fidelity** (utilities don't get stories, none added), **Real rendered-layout verification** (nothing renders), **React logic correctness** (no state/hooks/`useEffect` — that's step C3). Structure/Imports were folded into the cross-cutting sub-agent rather than run standalone. This is a first pass on a brand-new diff (six untracked files, never tested before) — nothing here is a re-run of unchanged work.

## Angle 1 — Gates, from scratch

All 9 checks CONFIRMED clean, via `general-purpose` sub-agent, real output:
- `npx tsc --noEmit` → exit 0, no output.
- **Baseline delta, proven not trusted**: sub-agent physically `git stash push -u`'d the six files, ran the full suite for a real "before" number (**79 files / 1190 tests, 0 failures**), popped, ran again (**82 files / 1228 tests, 0 failures**). Deltas: +3 files, +38 tests — matches the claimed numbers exactly, and matches via a method that can't be fooled by a stale self-report.
- Per-file split independently re-counted from `--reporter=verbose` output, no `test.each` trickery involved anywhere in these three files: **regionPrefCookie.test.ts = 21, crossSiteUrl.test.ts = 6, shouldShowLanguagePrompt.test.ts = 11** → 38 total. Exact match.
- `npm run audit:tokens` → still "3 unacknowledged violation(s)" (`overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts:20`, `.../zimmAuthDrawerContent/zimmAuthDrawerContent.css.ts:58`, `overrides/app/theme/components/zimmDrawerShared.ts:13`) — sub-agent read `scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`'s actual `SCAN_ROOTS` and confirmed `overrides/app/utils/` is structurally outside its scan roots, not just coincidentally clean. Unaffected by this step, as the plan predicted. 🔵 note: those 3 are real, pre-existing, unrelated to SFCC-831/689 — visibility only, not this step's fix.
- Zero `js-cookie` matches, zero `overrides/app/hooks/` import matches, zero 4+-level relative chains, no circular import (only edge is `shouldShowLanguagePrompt.ts → regionPrefCookie.ts`; `regionPrefCookie.ts` itself has **zero imports at all**, consistent with its isomorphic-purity claim).
- `git diff --stat package.json package-lock.json` → empty.
- All six filenames camelCase, correct convention for new Zimmermann-authored files.

## Angle 2 — `regionPrefCookie.ts` mutation testing

CONFIRMED clean, via sub-agent, with real red-then-green evidence:
- Wire format, `LANGUAGE_PROMPT_SUPPRESSION_DAYS = 7` (line 36), and the "pure half never touches `document`" claim all independently re-derived from the file, not assumed.
- **Mutation A** (`overrides/app/utils/regionPrefCookie.ts:138-142`, read-path try/catch removed): real run → exactly the "throwing getter... survived on read" test failed with an actual uncaught `DOMException`, 20/21 others stayed green. Restored, `diff` byte-identical, re-ran 21/21 green.
- **Mutation B** (`overrides/app/utils/regionPrefCookie.ts:163-167`, write-path try/catch removed): same rigor, exactly the "throwing setter... survived on write" test failed, restored, re-verified green.
- Both guards are load-bearing — the tests genuinely depend on them, not just co-exist with them.
- The 400-day `COOKIE_MAX_AGE_SECONDS` comment (`overrides/app/utils/regionPrefCookie.ts:40-50`) was quoted verbatim and confirmed to be a real, permanent, visible code comment explaining both the 400-day browser ceiling and the SFCC-823/REG-019 forward-looking risk — not something that exists only in a chat report.

## Angle 3 — `crossSiteUrl.ts` (I ran this myself)

CONFIRMED clean — and I caught and reversed my own false lead here before reporting it, worth stating plainly since self-correction is the whole point of this exercise:
- Verified directly against `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/url.js:118-163`: `getPathWithLocale(shortCode, buildUrl, opts={})` has no separate `path` parameter (reads `opts.location.pathname`/`.search` only) — matches the docstring's claim exactly. It also internally calls `getSiteByReference(siteRef)` using the **current URL's own** site reference, then scopes locale lookup to that same site — structurally incapable of targeting a different site, which is exactly why `crossSiteUrl.ts` exists and exactly why importing `getSiteByReference` itself would be pointless (target site/locale already arrive resolved). Both claims hold.
- Verified `BuildCrossSiteUrl`'s declared type against the **real** `buildUrl` in `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-multi-site.js:23-32` — signature `(path, siteRef, localeRef)` matches exactly. This mattered because `useMultiSite` ships untyped `.js` (per the plan's own C3 note), so `tsc` cannot catch a mismatch here — I checked it by hand since this step has no consumer yet to catch a wrong assumption at wiring time.
- I initially misread a citation — the plan text ("matching `footer/index.jsx:152`") is in `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-831/plan.md`, not in the shipped file. I grepped `overrides/app/utils/crossSiteUrl.ts`/`.test.ts` for "footer" directly: **zero matches**. The implementer wrote their own self-contained, accurate rationale for `DEFAULT_DISALLOWED_PARAMS = ['refine']` without citing any external file — there is no citation-accuracy defect in the deliverable. (For the record, since I'd already gone looking: the real precedent is `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/footer/index.jsx:152`, the base vendor footer, not the Zimmermann override — but since the shipped code never makes this citation, it isn't a finding against this step.)
- Ran 2 fail-on-purpose mutations myself: removed the bare-root-path normalisation (`overrides/app/utils/crossSiteUrl.ts:86-88`) → exactly the "collapses a bare site-root path" test failed (`expected '' to be '/'`), 5/6 others green; removed the `disallowParams.forEach` deletion (line 92) → exactly the 2 param-filtering tests failed with real leaking values (`refine`/`limit` surviving). Both restored byte-identical, both re-verified green.

## Angle 4 — `shouldShowLanguagePrompt.ts` branches, subtag, window math

CONFIRMED, one should-fix, one open design question. Via sub-agent:
- All six required branches present, each mapped to a distinct test, each asserting the **full** literal result shape via `toEqual` (not truthy/partial).
- **Throwaway `it-CH` test** (primary subtag `it`, uncovered by the existing suite) passed against the real implementation.
- **Stub-defeat mutation**: a narrowed `primarySubtag` that only special-cased `fr-fr`/`en-gb`/exact `it` still passed the **entire existing 11-test suite** — proof the existing suite alone cannot catch a hardcoded-for-the-demo-cases implementation. The new `it-CH` case then failed against that same stub. Restored byte-identical, both suites re-verified green, throwaway file deleted, `git status` confirmed clean.
- Window-math boundary arithmetic hand-verified correct; `LANGUAGE_PROMPT_SUPPRESSION_DAYS` confirmed imported (not redefined) everywhere.

**Finding 1 — 🟡 should-fix, CONFIRMED (by both me and the sub-agent independently), ONE-OFF.**
`overrides/app/utils/shouldShowLanguagePrompt.test.ts:65` — test named `'exactly the suppression-window boundary instant still counts as suppressed (now < end, not <=)'` asserts `{show: true, targetLanguage: 'fr'}` — i.e. the prompt **does** show, meaning the window is **not** active. The name says the opposite of what the test verifies. The logic, the arithmetic, and the inline comment two lines below are all correct — only the name string contradicts its own assertion. Violates `.claude/rules/testing.md`'s "test names describe the behaviour" rule. Low risk today, but this is exactly the file someone will reopen when negotiating the still-open 7-day-vs-indefinite question (plan.md open question #1), and a wrong name at that moment actively misleads.

**Note — 🔵, CONFIRMED as-coded, open product question, not a defect.**
`overrides/app/utils/shouldShowLanguagePrompt.ts:77` (`const browserLanguage = browserLanguages[0];`) only ever reads the browser's single most-preferred language. Plan.md never settles whether a shopper whose top preference isn't one of the four supported languages, but whose second preference is, should still get the prompt. Distinct from the already-tracked REG-030 open question (which is about geographic coverage, not preference-list depth) — worth a one-line confirmation from product before this reaches real multilingual shoppers.

## Against the ticket

Walked every checkbox in plan.md's Step C1 "Pass criteria" against the evidence above: tsc clean, 82/1228/0-failures, zero `js-cookie`, `package.json`/lock untouched, pure functions verified `document`-free, all cookie/crossSiteUrl/shouldShowLanguagePrompt test-coverage bullets verified present and meaningful (not just plausibly named), fail-on-purpose done for all three files (2 mutations each on regionPrefCookie and crossSiteUrl, a stronger stub-defeat mutation plus hand-verified arithmetic on shouldShowLanguagePrompt). Every criterion is met on real evidence, not on the strength of the implementer's own report.

## What I tried to falsify

Removed both try/catch guards in `regionPrefCookie.ts` (read and write) to see if their tests were decorative — they weren't. Removed `crossSiteUrl.ts`'s root-path normalisation and its param-filter to see if those tests were decorative — they weren't. Installed a narrow, hardcoded-looking `primarySubtag` stub in `shouldShowLanguagePrompt.ts` to see if the implementer's own 11-test suite would still pass against it — it did, which is exactly why the extra `it-CH` case was worth writing; that new case then caught what the original suite couldn't. Physically removed the six files via `git stash` to get a real "before" test count rather than trusting the claimed 79/1190 baseline. Read the actual vendor `node_modules` source for `getPathWithLocale`/`getSiteByReference`/`useMultiSite` rather than accepting the docstring's reasoning on faith — and in the process caught myself about to report a false finding (the "footer/index.jsx:152" citation lives in the plan document, not the shipped code) before it went into this report.

## What I could not verify

No rendered UI, browser, or Storybook surface exists in this step to check — genuinely vacuous, not skipped. I did not reproduce Safari private-mode behaviour in a real Safari instance; the tests simulate it via a mocked throwing getter/setter, which is this codebase's own established technique (cited from `useRecentlyViewedHistory.ts:30`) and is what the plan's pass criteria actually ask for. I did not check `npm run lint` — not in this step's pass criteria (only in the final-gate section, out of scope for a single-step test). The cookie's stated future SSR consumer (`request-processor.js`) doesn't exist yet, so nothing can test that end of the contract; this is explicitly deferred by the plan, not a gap in C1.

## What Marcel is missing

This cookie's wire format is about to become shared infrastructure for three more stories (SFCC-823/688/817) that haven't been built or reviewed yet, and it ships now through a Tier-4, no-review file — the `1|` version prefix is the only guaranteed-safe extension point if any of those three need a shape this format didn't anticipate (SFCC-817's still-unresolved "saved manual selection" AC is the most likely to need one). Worth a quick look from whoever picks up those stories before they treat this contract as settled rather than provisional.
